_comment: Quarantine (`rejected`) vectors for the OTA boot watchdog — SHIPPED and Android-device-verified 2026-07-25; see docs/ota-updates.md. Replayed by BOTH platforms (OtaCoreTests.swift and OtaCoreSelfTest.java) alongside ota-golden-vectors.json, and both must produce identical results. Kept as a separate file from the Phase 1 golden vectors only because it was authored as an adversarial-spike spec ahead of the implementation; the split has no runtime meaning.
_why: revert() currently erases pending/bootAttempts/confirmedBoots, leaving NO memory that a version was ever tried and failed. checkForUpdate compares the release's target only against `active` and `pending` (otaClient.ts:275), so the very next launch re-stages the SAME known-bad version. This infinite re-stage loop was directly OBSERVED on-device during Phase 1's iOS revert test (plan doc, iOS revert section step 4) and misread at the time as correct 'two-phase self-heal' — the cycle only ended because a human published a fix. Today it costs ~75% of launches; behind a mandatory gate it is a permanent, unrecoverable brick.

scenarios.name: revert_after_max_attempts_QUARANTINES_the_bad_version
scenarios._note: The headline fix. Attempt exhaustion is PROOF the bundle failed to boot 3 separate times, so the version is recorded in `rejected` and must never be staged again by this device.

scenarios.name: revert_to_embedded_also_quarantines
scenarios._note: Same rule when there is no active version to fall back to (fresh install whose FIRST update is broken — exactly the iOS v7 case observed on-device).

scenarios.name: missing_pending_folder_reverts_WITHOUT_quarantine
scenarios._note: Deliberate asymmetry, and the subtlest decision in this spike. A missing staged folder is NOT proof the bundle is bad — the OS may have cleared it under disk pressure, or a partial stage was cleaned up. Re-staging is the CORRECT heal here, so quarantining would permanently block a perfectly good version over a transient disk event. Only attempt-exhaustion (the scenario above) is proof of badness.

scenarios.name: quarantine_list_is_capped_oldest_dropped
scenarios._note: Unbounded growth in a file read on every cold boot is a slow leak. FIFO cap at maxRejectedPerBundle; dropping the OLDEST is safe because re-staging an ancient version requires the CDN to still advertise it, which the publisher controls.

scenarios.name: boot_NEVER_consults_rejected_for_an_already_active_version
scenarios._note: Load-bearing separation of concerns: `rejected` is a STAGING-side gate (read by checkForUpdate + the mandatory gate in JS), never a BOOT-side one. If a version somehow reached `active`, it booted successfully twice and must keep booting — letting the quarantine list veto it here could strand a device with nothing to run.

scenarios.name: unknown_rejected_field_in_old_state_json_parses_as_empty
scenarios._note: Forward/backward compat: a device updating from a Phase 1/2 binary has a state.json with no `rejected` key at all. Must parse to an empty map, never nil-crash — same contract as every other field.
